function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t something that was “discovered” by a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. The modern scientific understanding of electricity developed over centuries through the work of many thinkers:

| Era | Key Contributors | Contribution |
|-----|------------------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | Thales of Miletus | Noted static electricity from rubbing amber (Greek *elektron*). |
| **17th–18th Century** | William Gilbert | Distinguished between magnetism and static electricity; coined the term *electricus*. |
| **18th Century** | Benjamin Franklin | Proposed the concept of positive and negative charges; conducted the famous kite experiment. |
| **Late 18th Century** | Alessandro Volta | Invented the voltaic pile (first battery), providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Early 19th Century** | Luigi Galvani & Alessandro Volta | Galvani studied bioelectricity; Volta developed the galvanic cell. |
| **Early 19th Century** | Michael Faraday | Discovered electromagnetic induction; laid groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **Mid 19th Century** | James Clerk Maxwell | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations, predicting electromagnetic waves. |

So while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these scientists—and many others—led to our modern understanding and practical use of electrical phenomena.
